newsitem.title: USA: Chevron to end California oil output - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Chevron to end California oil output - WSJ.

text.p: U.S. oil company Chevron Corp plans to end all offshore crude oil production in California between 1999 and 2001, years sooner than it had originally planned, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.

The newspaper cited company officials as saying Chevron and partners Phillips Petroleum Co and Texaco Inc will have pumped oil out of the Point Arguello for about 10 years instead of the 25 years that they had originally projected.
Chevron, which has a 26-percent interest in the field, expected to recover about 140 million barrels of oil, one third of the total economically recoverable oil envisioned in the beginning, it said.
The newspaper said the field's production had fallen to 30,000 barrels a day from an average 60,000 in 1995.
It cited Chevron's filing to the Securities and Exchange Commission as saying it expected an "additional impairment write-down may result" from the field's rapid decline.
Company officials declined to say how big the impairment would be.
The officials blamed state regulatory and environmental hurdles as the reason for their loss of interest in the project.
